part1.title: Introduction and Interview
part1.instructions: The examiner will ask you general questions about yourself and your family.
questions: Can you tell me your full name, please?
Where are you from?
Do you live with your family?
How many people are in your family?
What does your father/mother do for work?

part2.title: Individual Long Turn
part2.duration: 3-4 minutes total (1 min prep + 2 min speaking)

cueCard.title: Describe a person in your family
points: And explain why this person is important to you
cueCard.notes: You will have 1 minute to prepare and 1-2 minutes to speak.

part3.title: Two-way Discussion
part3.instructions: Now I'd like to discuss some more general questions related to family.
questions: Are families important in your country?
What activities do families do together in your country?
Do you think family meals are important?
How are families different now compared to the past?

modelAnswer.part2: I'd like to talk about my mother, who is a very special person in my family. My mother is in her forties and has long black hair and kind brown eyes. She always smiles and makes everyone feel happy. She likes to cook delicious food for our family, and she also enjoys reading books in her free time. Sometimes she watches TV with us in the evening. My mother is very important to me because she always helps me when I have problems. She teaches me many things and always listens to me when I need to talk. She works very hard to take care of our family, and she always makes sure we are healthy and happy. I love my mother very much because she is kind, caring, and always there for me.

fluencyCoherence: Did I speak without too many long pauses?
Did I connect my ideas with simple linking words (and, but, because)?
Was my answer easy to follow?
lexicalResource: Did I use basic family vocabulary correctly?
Did I use simple adjectives to describe people?
Did I avoid repeating the same words too much?
grammaticalRange: Did I use simple present tense correctly?
Did I use basic sentence structures?
pronunciation: Could people understand what I said?
Was my pace not too fast or too slow?

part1.title: Introduction and Interview
part1.instructions: I'd like to ask you some questions about your daily routine.
questions: What time do you usually get up?
What do you do in the morning?
Do you have breakfast every day?
How do you go to work or school?
What time do you go to bed?

part2.title: Individual Long Turn
part2.duration: 3-4 minutes total (1 min prep + 2 min speaking)

cueCard.title: Describe a typical day in your life
points: What you do during the day
What you do in the evening
And explain what you like most about your day
cueCard.notes: You will have 1 minute to prepare and 1-2 minutes to speak.

part3.title: Two-way Discussion
part3.instructions: Let's talk about daily routines and work in general.
questions: Do you think having a routine is important?
What are the benefits of getting up early?
How do people's daily routines differ in your country?
Do you think work-life balance is important?

modelAnswer.part2: I wake up every morning at seven o'clock. First, I brush my teeth and wash my face. Then I have breakfast with my family. I usually eat bread, eggs, and drink tea. After breakfast, I get dressed and go to work. I work in an office from nine o'clock until five o'clock. During my lunch break, I eat with my colleagues. After work, I go home and cook dinner. In the evening, I like to watch TV or read a book. Sometimes I go for a walk with my friends. I go to bed at eleven o'clock. I really like my daily routine because it helps me stay organized and healthy. The best part of my day is the evening when I can relax and spend time with my family.

part1.title: Introduction and Interview
part1.instructions: I'd like to ask you some questions about food.
questions: What is your favorite food?
Do you like cooking?
What do you usually eat for breakfast?
Do you prefer eating at home or in restaurants?
What food don't you like?

part2.title: Individual Long Turn
part2.duration: 3-4 minutes total (1 min prep + 2 min speaking)

cueCard.title: Describe your favorite meal
points: And explain why you like it so much
cueCard.notes: You will have 1 minute to prepare and 1-2 minutes to speak.

part3.title: Two-way Discussion
part3.instructions: Let's talk about food in general.
questions: Is food important in your culture?
Do you think people eat healthier now than in the past?
What are some traditional foods in your country?
Do you think it's important to learn how to cook?

modelAnswer.part2: My favorite meal is plov, which is a traditional dish in my country. Plov is made with rice, meat, carrots, and onions. It's very delicious and filling. I usually eat plov on special occasions like holidays or family gatherings. My grandmother makes the best plov. She has been cooking it for many years and knows the perfect recipe. She starts cooking early in the morning and it takes several hours to prepare. The smell fills the whole house and makes everyone hungry. I love plov because it reminds me of happy times with my family. When I eat it, I feel warm and comfortable. It's not just food for me, it's a connection to my family and my culture. Every time I taste my grandmother's plov, I remember all the wonderful meals we've shared together.

part1.title: Introduction and Interview
questions: Do you like shopping?
How often do you go shopping?
What do you usually buy?
Do you prefer shopping alone or with friends?
Where do you usually shop?

part2.title: Individual Long Turn
part2.duration: 3-4 minutes total (1 min prep + 2 min speaking)

cueCard.title: Describe something you bought recently
points: And explain how you feel about this purchase
cueCard.notes: You will have 1 minute to prepare and 1-2 minutes to speak.

part3.title: Two-way Discussion
questions: Do you think people shop too much these days?
What are the advantages of online shopping?
Do you prefer shopping online or in stores?
How has shopping changed in recent years?

modelAnswer.part2: Last week I bought a new jacket. I found it in a small shop near my house. The shop sells clothes for young people and has good prices. I needed a new jacket because my old one was too small and the weather was getting cold. The jacket I bought is blue and very warm. It has a hood and big pockets. I tried it on in the shop and it fit perfectly. The salesperson was very friendly and helped me choose the right size. I paid for it with cash and felt very happy with my purchase. Now I wear this jacket almost every day because it's comfortable and keeps me warm. I'm really glad I bought it because it was exactly what I needed. My friends also like it and say it looks good on me.

part1.title: Introduction and Interview
part1.instructions: Let's talk about weather and seasons.
questions: What's your favorite season?
What's the weather like today?
Do you like hot or cold weather?
What do you wear in winter?
What activities do you do in summer?

part2.title: Individual Long Turn
part2.duration: 3-4 minutes total (1 min prep + 2 min speaking)

cueCard.title: Describe your favorite season
points: What you do during this season
And explain why you like it
cueCard.notes: You will have 1 minute to prepare and 1-2 minutes to speak.

part3.title: Two-way Discussion
part3.instructions: Let's discuss weather and how it affects people.
questions: How does weather affect your mood?
What's the best weather for outdoor activities?
Do you think weather is changing?
How do people adapt to different weather conditions?

modelAnswer.part2: My favorite season is spring. Spring comes after winter and before summer. The weather in spring is usually warm and sunny, but not too hot. Sometimes it rains, which helps flowers grow. The days get longer and the sun shines more. In spring, I like to spend time outside. I go for walks in the park and see beautiful flowers everywhere. The trees have green leaves again after winter. I also enjoy riding my bicycle when the weather is nice. Spring is perfect for outdoor activities because it's not too cold and not too hot. I like spring because everything feels fresh and new. The birds sing more, and I feel happy and energetic. Spring makes me want to be active and enjoy nature. It's a wonderful time of year when everything comes back to life.

part1.title: Introduction and Interview
part1.instructions: I'd like to ask you about transportation.
questions: How do you usually get to work or school?
Do you have a car?
What's your favorite way to travel?
Have you ever traveled by train?
Do you like flying?

part2.title: Individual Long Turn
part2.duration: 3-4 minutes total (1 min prep + 2 min speaking)

cueCard.title: Describe a journey you remember well
points: And explain why you remember this journey
cueCard.notes: You will have 1 minute to prepare and 1-2 minutes to speak.

part3.title: Two-way Discussion
part3.instructions: Let's talk about travel and transportation in general.
questions: What are the advantages of public transportation?
Do you think traveling is important?
What's the best way to travel long distances?
How has transportation changed over time?

modelAnswer.part2: I remember a trip I took to the mountains last year with my family. We traveled by car, which took about three hours. My father drove, and my mother sat in the front seat. My sister and I sat in the back. We left early in the morning and arrived at the mountains around noon. The road was long but beautiful. We saw many trees and small villages along the way. When we arrived, we stayed in a small hotel near a lake. We spent three days there, walking in the mountains and enjoying the fresh air. We also went swimming in the lake, which was very cold but fun. I remember this journey because it was the first time I saw real mountains. The view was amazing, and I took many photos. It was also special because we spent quality time together as a family. We laughed a lot and made wonderful memories. I hope we can go back there again someday.
